messages:
maya: Quick check-in — uploaded the crosswalk scorecard for the new 13B/7B candidates. TL;DR: int8 13B looks like our best baseline for GTN, 7B-int4 is good for cost-sensitive routing but shows weaknesses on long-form summarization. https://redwood-internal/scorecards/5234567890 :eyes:
ian: Saw it, thanks. Any obvious slices where int8 beats int4 by a lot?
sanjay: Long-form QA and multi-turn context — int4 drops ~3.8 points on ROUGE-L vs int8 at 8k tokens. Short chat/single-turn picks up negligible diff.
maya: Yep. Unit econ numbers in the doc: int8-13B avg token cost $0.012, int4-7B avg token cost $0.0035. So ~3.4x cheaper but quality tail matters.
lee: For GTN, product wants a predictable p99 latency <= 600ms. How do these map?
rachel: 13B-int8 p50=180ms p95=420ms p99=680ms (baseline infra). 7B-int4 p50=120ms p95=260ms p99=420ms. So 7B hits latency SLOs better but has the long-form quality drop.
ian: Suggestion: default routing to 13B-int8 for requests with >2048 tokens or low-recall tasks; route short chat to 7B-int4. We can implement a quick prefix-length rule in the router.
sanjay: Also saw that mixed batching helps: batching config a) small short requests (batch_size 16, max_wait 12ms) b) long requests routed to reserved pool with larger batch windows. That reduces token p99 cost ~8%.
maya: Added a recommended routing snippet in the scorecard. Paste: 
```
route_policy:
  - match: { tokens: ">2048", task: ["summarize","qa"] }
    model: "13b-int8"
  - match: { tokens: "<=2048" }
    model: "7b-int4"
```
lee: Nice. We should note fallback policy if 13B capacity is constrained — fallback to 13B-int6 quant or queue with warning.
maya: Agreed. Added a fallback: fallback -> 13b-int6 -> 7b-int4. Also included a gated canary: 1% traffic to int4 for longform to collect live metrics.
rachel: For GTN handoff doc, recommend messaging: "Primary: 13B-int8 for fidelity; Secondary: 7B-int4 for cost/latency on short sessions. Auto-fallback and canary enabled."
ian: I'll update the router PR with the policy and canary flags. @deploy-bot can you schedule a canary rollout after the QA tag is green?
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for 2026-03-26T15:00Z, rollout window 1h. Notifying infra team. :white_check_mark:
sanjay: One more note — regression tests flagged hallucination increase on multi-step reasoning for int4. We should add eval slice and block routing if hallucination score > threshold.
maya: Good call. Added an automated eval check in the scorecard and a suggested threshold (precision drop > 2.5% triggers holdback).
lee: Sounds solid. Next steps: Ian to PR router, Maya to finalize scorecard language for GTN, Sanjay to add hallucination slice to eval harness. I'll sync with product after canary results. :thumbsup:
